key_insight: Neutron-irradiated CdS/CdTe solar cells show persistent performance losses after 18 months, with partial recovery during short annealing but fill-factor degradation during prolonged treatment.
engineering_relevance: Radiation-tolerant CdTe space photovoltaics require coordinated optimization of substrates, absorbers, contacts, and recovery treatments.
method: Irradiate cells for 10–150 min in a 90 kW TRIGA reactor at nominal neutron fluences of 3.3 × 10^14–5.0 × 10^15 n/cm².
Characterize device performance and co-irradiated FTO-coated glass after 18 months of storage.
Evaluate recovery by annealing at 70 °C under one-sun illumination.
evidence_signal: FTO-coated glass transmission at 500 nm fell from 80% to 50% after 60 min of irradiation; annealed cells reached their highest efficiency after 4 h.
watch_item: Defect mechanisms remain unresolved, and delayed characterization does not establish immediate post-irradiation performance or in-orbit recovery.
paper_title: Persistent Neutron Irradiation Effects and Partial Recovery in Thin-Film CdS/CdTe Solar Cells
